major.title: The guard still accepts holder blocks whose reprint is not a faithful rendering: the 6.0 printer emits no parentheses, so every compound expression without an explicit `Parens` op reparses to a different tree under parser 0.2.0's precedence layers (or not at all); an empty `Term::Bytes` prints as `hex:` which the parser rejects; `All`/`Any` in binary form print as `.any(true)` which the parser rejects — SECURITY.md step 5 (line 30-31) still claims the class is rejected
major.detail: src/authorize.rs:452 `Op::Unary(_) | Op::Binary(_) => true` and :436 `Term::Bytes(_) => true` pass these constructs. The printer (third_party/…/src/datalog/expression.rs:540-580, :132-143) renders `Binary::print(left, right)` as `left op right` with no grouping; only an explicit `Unary::Parens` op yields `( … )`. The parser (biscuit-parser-0.2.0 parser.rs:502-640) is a precedence-climbing parser (`||` < `&&` < comparisons, non-associative at expr2:524-542 < `|` < `^` < `&` < `+ -` < `* /` < `!` binding expr6 < methods), so a stack program whose evaluation order differs from that precedence prints as a string that reparses to another program. Empirical, holder-appended block 2 (no root key), token ACCEPTED by the guard and by evaluation, reprint re-signed as a fresh block 2: `[1, 2, Add, 3, Mul, 9, Equal]` -> ACCEPT(policy=0), printed `check if 1 + 2 * 3 === 9;`, reparsed `[1, 2, 3, Mul, Add, 9, Equal]` (= 7 === 9), reprint -> DENY(auth.operation_denied); `[6, 2, 1, Sub, Sub, 5, Equal]` (6-(2-1)=5) -> ACCEPT, printed `6 - 2 - 1 === 5`, reprint -> DENY; `[1, 3, 2, BitwiseXor, BitwiseAnd, 1, Equal]` -> ACCEPT, printed `1 & 3 ^ 2 === 1`, reparsed as `(1 & 3) ^ 2`, reprint -> DENY; `[2, 3, Mul, TypeOf, "integer", Equal]` -> ACCEPT, printed `2 * 3.type() === "integer"`, reprint -> DENY; `[true, false, Equal, Negate]` -> ACCEPT, printed `!true === false`, reparsed `[true, Negate, false, Equal]` (same value, different tree); `[1, 2, LessThan, true, Equal]` -> ACCEPT, printed `1 < 2 === true`, PARSE-ERROR (comparisons are non-associative); `[Bytes([]), Bytes([]), Equal]` -> ACCEPT, printed `hex: === hex:`, PARSE-ERROR (parse_bytes = take_while1, parser.rs:765-777); `[{1}, true, Any]` and `[{1}, true, All]` -> guard passes, printed `{1}.any(true)` / `{1}.all(true)`, PARSE-ERROR (binary_method requires `$x ->`, parser.rs:656-665), denied only by evaluation (auth.operation_denied) — the same closure-inserted-on-reparse class the round rejected for `TryOr`/`LazyAnd`/`LazyOr` (doc comment src/authorize.rs:408-411 names those three and omits `All`/`Any`). Impact on the decision: none found — blocks 0 and 1 are matched on exact op slices (`canonical_operation_check`/`exact_expiration_check`), block 2 is never reprinted by this crate, and the value divergences above only make the *reprint* stricter or unparsable. What is wrong is the guarantee text: SECURITY.md:30-31 'Reject any token whose decoded terms would not survive the pinned print/parse round trip unchanged' is a blanket claim contradicted by these accepted tokens, while SECURITY.md:149-150 says constructs outside the two lists are 'not claimed either way' — the two sentences cannot both hold. Either the guard rejects every op sequence that is not a single precedence-conformant tree (or requires `Parens` around every compound operand; or rejects `All`/`Any`/`Get` in binary form and empty bytes), or step 5 is reworded to the exact lists and the record's 'CONFIRMED, closed' for this class is downgraded to 'four instances closed'.

minor.title: P-256 signature verification is reachable from untrusted token bytes: a third-party block signed with a Secp256r1 external key is accepted, and a rule-level `trusting secp256r1/<hex>` scope round-trips and is accepted — the Ed25519-only boundary now enforced at the key entry points does not cover the chain, contrary to SECURITY.md step 3 and to the round-1 residual 'inert unless supplied by configuration'
minor.detail: SECURITY.md:11-15 restricts the *configured* keys to Ed25519 and :28 says 'Verify the Ed25519 signature and Biscuit chain'. biscuit-auth 6.0 verifies each third-party block with the algorithm-tagged public key carried in the block itself (third_party/…/src/token/mod.rs:411-435, `PublicKey::from_proto(&external_signature.public_key)`), so a token holder can make the verifier execute the ecdsa/p256 code path by appending a P-256-signed block; no configuration is involved. Empirical: `R1 third-party[p256] blocks=3 ext_key_alg=Some(1) -> ACCEPT(policy=0)` (Algorithm 1 = Secp256r1), `R1 block1-as-third-party[p256] -> ACCEPT(policy=0)`, `R2 block2 rule-scope[p256] printed=`check if true trusting secp256r1/03fc…;` parsed_scopes=Ok(PublicKey { algorithm: Secp256r1 }) -> ACCEPT(policy=0)`. No escalation: a third-party block can only add checks, and a P-256 *root* is refused (`R5 p256-root-token vs ed25519 ring -> DENY(auth.biscuit_invalid)`). What is inaccurate is the attack-surface statement: the 17-crate P-256 chain added in 6.0 (round-1 minor 4) is exercised by unauthenticated input, and the crate has no switch to refuse non-Ed25519 external keys (an `external_key.algorithm != Ed25519` check on `snapshot().world.blocks[*].external_key` would close it in the same structural pass as the scope check).

nonBlocking.detail: The record's mutant table names tests that exist in tests/authz.rs (guard_* 22 tests, block_level_scopes…, non_ed25519_keys…, term_parameter_never…); the mutation replay itself (26 mutants) was not re-executed here — the table is the author's claim. SECURITY.md:121-139 rejected list: each bullet maps to a guard arm (:430-452, :486-492) and to a probe or author test. SECURITY.md:141-144 'unreachable' claims for Term::Parameter and the policy walk are consistent with the code (`token.authorizer()` holds no policy). The record's own 'Not done' list (:191-207) matches what this pass found still open, except the precedence/empty-bytes/All-Any class, which it does not mention.

residualRisks: Print/parse injectivity for holder blocks (block 2+) is bounded by the exact lists in SECURITY.md:107-139 and nothing else: any compound expression without explicit `Parens`, empty bytes, and `All`/`Any`/`Get` in binary form are accepted by the guard with a reprint that is stricter, different or unparsable. No consumer of the block-2 reprint exists in this crate today; a future audit/log feature that prints holder blocks would show something other than what was evaluated.
SECURITY.md:30-31 (step 5) and :149-150 make contradictory statements about coverage; a reader of step 5 alone believes a guarantee the code does not provide.

P-256 signature verification and rule-level `secp256r1/` scopes are reachable from token bytes through third-party blocks; the round-1 assessment that the P-256 chain is inert is withdrawn. No escalation was found (third-party blocks only add checks).

The provenance gate proves tree == archive + committed diff; 'committed diff == upstream #306' is a review fact re-verified in this pass, not a gate fact. Content-only comparison (modes/symlinks not compared).
The 26-mutant replay reported in the evidence record was not re-executed by this pass; the killing-test names were checked to exist.
Rolling deployment (a 5.0.0-issued token authorizing under 6.0.0) remains asserted by reading only, as in round 1.
This pass ran on macOS; Linux CI legs are taken from the GitHub check rollup and job log on d65e877.
